title: Patagonia Wave Editing: Leading Lines, Compositional Tension, and Two-Image Blending

date.basis: embedded_creation_time metadata; transcript does not confirm actual production date

locations.name: Patagonia (probable)
locations.basis: filename and folder context reference Patagonia; transcript contains no explicit shooting location

summary: This editing-focused segment guides the viewer through a landscape workflow centered on sea-wave imagery. The presenter outlines baseline exposure and color adjustments to keep tones subdued, then evaluates multiple wave samples to establish a clear leading line. They discuss testing composites from two RAW frames, noting alignment challenges caused by waves moving the tripod. The workflow introduces a clone-stamp-based test for alignment, emphasizes compositional tension by favoring odd-number focal structures, and concludes with cropping and background considerations to favor atmosphere over busy foreground. The transcript captures practical decision points rather than a full step-by-step tutorial.

sections.title: Initial exposure and color tweaks
sections.description: Describes lifting shadows/blacks, slightly lowering exposure, adjusting whites, and cooling color tone to avoid brightness overload; serves as a baseline for later edits.

sections.title: Wave selection and leading lines
sections.description: Considers multiple wave shots and emphasizes creating a strong leading line to guide the viewer's eye; avoids cluttered foreground by limiting overlaid elements.

sections.title: Two-shot RAW blending considerations
sections.description: Explores blending two RAW frames, with note that alignment may be compromised by tripod movement and wave-induced camera motion.

sections.title: Testing blend with clone alignment
sections.description: Demonstrates using a clone-stamp approach to test how two images might blend; discusses techniques to align the blend within the scene.

sections.title: Compositional tension and focal points
sections.description: Introduces the idea that even-numbered focal points create tension; advocates for odd-numbered arrangements to keep the eye moving and avoid multiple equal focal points.

sections.title: Cropping and background considerations
sections.description: Considers how moving the background and cropping the bottom can enhance atmosphere; identifies preference for a strongest single shot.

featured_techniques.technique: Leading lines created by wave slope to guide viewer's eye
Compositional tension: favor odd-number focal points
